topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series, its audience and the learning outcomes for this lecture.

topics.label: Accumulating genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the stepwise accumulation of cellular changes as a model of cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer as disrupted differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer through the loss of normal tissue organization and show why studying isolated cells cannot fully capture that disruption.

topics.label: Invasion and metastasis in malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how malignant tumors differ from benign tumors through their invasion of surrounding tissue and capacity for spread to distant sites.

topics.label: Benign tumors: progression and clinical risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical significance of benign tumors, whose potential for malignant progression varies and whose non-invasive status does not guarantee harmlessness.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor growth and dissemination compromise normal bodily function and ultimately cause death.

topics.label: Patterns of tumor incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare how tumor frequency varies by tissue of origin across human populations and animal species.

topics.label: Cancer detection and screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the need for early detection and why screening succeeds or falls short depending on the tumor and the available test.

topics.label: Lecture close and next steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by directing students to revision, supervisory discussions and upcoming practicals.
